s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful swelling and muscle weakness with systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the calves
Elevated LDH and CK
Diffuse subcutaneous edema on CT scan
Muscle biopsy showing interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
Cardiac involvement with myocarditis and atrial fibrillation
Neurologic involvement with somnolence, personality changes, and a hyperintense lesion on spinal MRI
key_facts: 57-year-old man with stage cS4a mantle cell lymphoma in complete remission
Presented with painful swelling of the calves in August 2018
No evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection
Brief gastroenteritis episode at the time of presentation
Diuretics gave transient relief
Systemic steroids and discontinuation of ibrutinib had no effect
Elevated LDH and CK on laboratory tests
Negative autoimmune serology
CT scan showed no lymphoma relapse but diffuse subcutaneous edema
ECOG performance status 3 at the time of hospitalization
Elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH on laboratory tests
Reduced plasma protein, albumin, and IgG
Elevated leukocyte count
MRI of the thighs showed diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema
Muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
Developed acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis
Troponin I rose further
ECG revealed a new right bundle branch block and repolarization disturbances
Developed atrial fibrillation
Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis
Increasing somnolence and personality changes were noted
Brain MRI was unremarkable
Spinal MRI demonstrated a hyperintense lesion concerning for myelitis
CSF analysis showed leukocyte count 329/μl, lactate 3.5 mmol/L, and protein 79.6 mg/dl

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CK, muscle biopsy with interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates, and clinical presentation of muscle weakness and pain

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to polymyositis, but skin involvement not explicitly mentioned in the case context

shortlist.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CK, muscle biopsy with necrosis, and clinical presentation of rapid progression of muscle weakness

shortlist.label: Ibrutinib-induced myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was taking ibrutinib, which is known to cause myopathy, and discontinued use did not improve symptoms

shortlist.label: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of muscle inflammation and weakness, with negative autoimmune serology and no clear underlying cause

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms began after receiving ibrutinib, and the condition worsened despite discontinuation of the drug, which suggests a potential link between ibrutinib and the patient's myopathy

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: While the patient's muscle biopsy showed interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates, the temporal association with ibrutinib initiation and the lack of other characteristic features of polymyositis make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: There is no mention of characteristic skin manifestations, such as Gottron's papules or heliotrope rash, which are typically seen in dermatomyositis

rejected.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
rejected.why: While the patient's muscle biopsy showed necrosis and regeneration, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not strongly support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy
rejected.why: The patient's condition is more likely related to ibrutinib use, given the temporal association and the lack of other characteristic features of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy
